title: Build in public, fail in public: what it’s like to be a founder under 20 right now
slides: Why would a teen founder broadcast their biggest failure live?
Building in public means sharing revenue drops instantly.
But one viral mistake scared off my first five investors.
You now pivot before the trolls even finish commenting.
Stop curating; post your ugliest dashboard screenshot today.
thread_text:
1. Why broadcast failure live?

A teen founder streamed revenue data and instantly lost five investors.

2. Building in public backfired.

The same transparency that attracted followers pushed away funding.

3. A single mistake changed everything.

One viral screenshot turned supporters into critics before the meeting ended.

4. Pivot faster than the trolls.

Reaction time dropped from weeks to hours. Every comment now forces a product change.

5. Post your ugliest dashboard today.

Take one screenshot of your worst metric this week and share it publicly. What do you have to lose?
video_script: One viral mistake scared them off.

The same transparency that grows an audience can kill your funding round.

Now reaction time drops from weeks to hours—trolls force pivot decisions before you finish reading comments.

Would you post your ugliest dashboard screenshot this week, or does the risk outweigh the followers? 🚨
